questions.explanation_text: $\begin{aligned} & \sqrt{1+x^{2}}+x=sec\theta+tan\theta=t \\ & \sqrt{1+x^{2}}=sec\theta=\frac{t^{2}+1}{2t} \\ & x=tan\theta=\frac{t^{2}-1}{2t} \end{aligned}$ The given expression becomes $\frac{1}{m}t^{2}(n \cdot \frac{t^{2}+1}{2t}-\frac{t^{2}-1}{2t})=\frac{t^{n-1}}{2m}((n-1)t^{2}+n+1)$ By compare $\begin{aligned} & n=19 \\ & m=360 \\ & \therefore n+m=379 \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:

questions.question_text: If $\int \frac{2x^{2}+5x+9}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}dx=x\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\alpha\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\beta log_{e}|x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}|+C$ , where $C$ is the constant of integration, then $\alpha+2\beta$ is equal to __________ .
questions.question_html: If $\int \frac{2x^{2}+5x+9}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}dx=x\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\alpha\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\beta log_{e}|x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}|+C$ , where $C$ is the constant of integration, then $\alpha+2\beta$ is equal to __________ .
questions.explanation_html:
$\begin{aligned} & 2x^{2}+5x+9=A(x^{2}+x+1)+B(2x+1)+C \\ & A=2B=\frac{3}{2}C=\frac{11}{2} \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & 2\int \sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}dx+\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}}dx+\frac{11}{2}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}} \\ & 2\int \sqrt{⎷(x+\frac{1}{2})^{2}+(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})^{2}}dx+3\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\frac{11}{2}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(x+\frac{1}{2})^{2}+(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})^{2}}} \\ & 2(\frac{x+\frac{1}{2}}{2}\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}+\frac{3}{8}\ell n(x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}))+3\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1} \\ & +\frac{11}{2}\ell n(x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1})+C \\ & \alpha=\frac{7}{2} \\ & \alpha+2\beta=16 \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: If $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{}}dx=A(\frac{\alpha x-1}{\beta x+3})^{B}+C$ , where $C$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $\alpha+\beta+20AB$ is _________.
questions.explanation_text: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{}}dx \\ & \frac{x+3}{x-1}=t \Rightarrow dx=\frac{-4}{(t-1)^{2}}dt \Rightarrow x=(\frac{3+t}{t-1}) \\ & \Rightarrow (x-1)^{4}(x+3)^{6}=(x-1)^{5}(x+3)^{5}(\frac{x+3}{x-1}) \\ & I=\int \frac{\frac{-4}{(t-1)^{2}}dt}{t^{1/5}(\frac{3+t}{t-1}-1)(\frac{3+t}{t-3}+3)} \\ & I=\int \frac{-4dt}{t^{1/5}(16t)}=\frac{5}{4}(\frac{x-1}{x+3})^{1/5}+c \end{aligned}$ Comparing, $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow A=\frac{5}{4},B=\frac{1}{5},\alpha=1,\beta=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha+\beta+20AB=1+1+20 \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{1}{5}=7 \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
$\begin{aligned} & I=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{}}dx \\ & \frac{x+3}{x-1}=t \Rightarrow dx=\frac{-4}{(t-1)^{2}}dt \Rightarrow x=(\frac{3+t}{t-1}) \\ & \Rightarrow (x-1)^{4}(x+3)^{6}=(x-1)^{5}(x+3)^{5}(\frac{x+3}{x-1}) \\ & I=\int \frac{\frac{-4}{(t-1)^{2}}dt}{t^{1/5}(\frac{3+t}{t-1}-1)(\frac{3+t}{t-3}+3)} \\ & I=\int \frac{-4dt}{t^{1/5}(16t)}=\frac{5}{4}(\frac{x-1}{x+3})^{1/5}+c \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: If $\int cosec^{5}xdx=\alpha cotxcosecx(cosec^{2}x+\frac{3}{2})+\beta log_{x}|tan\frac{x}{2}|+C$ where $\alpha,\beta \in ℝ$ and $C$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $8(\alpha+\beta)$ equals _________.
questions.explanation_text: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int (cosecx)^{5}dx=\int (cosecx)^{3}(cosecx)^{2}dx \\ & =(cosecx)^{3}\int cosec^{2}xdx- \\ & \int (\frac{d}{dx}(cosecx)^{3}\int cosec^{2}xdx)dx \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-\int 3cosec^{2}x \cdot (-cosecxcotx)(-cotx)dx \\ & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-\int 3cosec^{3}xcot^{2}xdx \\ & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-3\int (cosecx)^{3}(cosec^{2}x-1)dx \\ & I=-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-3I+3\int (cosecx)^{3}dx \\ & 4I=-cotx(cosecx)^{3}+3\int (cosecx)^{3}dx \\ & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}+3I_{1} \\ & I_{1}=\int cosecx \cdot cosec^{2}xdx=cosecx(-cotx)- \\ & \int (-cosecxcotx)(-cotx)dx \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & I_{1}=-cosecxcotx-\int cosecx(cosec^{2}x-1)dx \\ & I_{1}=-cosecxcotx-I+\int cosecxdx \\ & 2l_{1}=-cosecxcotx+ln|tan\frac{x}{2}| \\ & \Rightarrow 4l=-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-\frac{3}{2}cosecxcotx+\frac{3}{2}ln|tan\frac{x}{2}|+C \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & I=-\frac{1}{4}cosecxcotx(cosec^{2}x+\frac{3}{2})+\frac{3}{8}ln|tan\frac{x}{2}|+C \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=-\frac{1}{4},\beta=\frac{3}{8} \Rightarrow 8(\alpha+\beta)=1 \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
$\begin{aligned} & I=\int (cosecx)^{5}dx=\int (cosecx)^{3}(cosecx)^{2}dx \\ & =(cosecx)^{3}\int cosec^{2}xdx- \\ & \int (\frac{d}{dx}(cosecx)^{3}\int cosec^{2}xdx)dx \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-\int 3cosec^{2}x \cdot (-cosecxcotx)(-cotx)dx \\ & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-\int 3cosec^{3}xcot^{2}xdx \\ & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-3\int (cosecx)^{3}(cosec^{2}x-1)dx \\ & I=-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-3I+3\int (cosecx)^{3}dx \\ & 4I=-cotx(cosecx)^{3}+3\int (cosecx)^{3}dx \\ & =-cotx(cosecx)^{3}+3I_{1} \\ & I_{1}=\int cosecx \cdot cosec^{2}xdx=cosecx(-cotx)- \\ & \int (-cosecxcotx)(-cotx)dx \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & I_{1}=-cosecxcotx-\int cosecx(cosec^{2}x-1)dx \\ & I_{1}=-cosecxcotx-I+\int cosecxdx \\ & 2l_{1}=-cosecxcotx+ln|tan\frac{x}{2}| \\ & \Rightarrow 4l=-cotx(cosecx)^{3}-\frac{3}{2}cosecxcotx+\frac{3}{2}ln|tan\frac{x}{2}|+C \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & I=-\frac{1}{4}cosecxcotx(cosec^{2}x+\frac{3}{2})+\frac{3}{8}ln|tan\frac{x}{2}|+C \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=-\frac{1}{4},\beta=\frac{3}{8} \Rightarrow 8(\alpha+\beta)=1 \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: Let $f(x)=\int \frac{dx}{(3+4x^{2})\sqrt{4-3x^{2}}},|x|<\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ . If $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}tan^{-1}(\frac{\alpha}{\beta})$ , $\alpha,\beta>0$ , then $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}$ is equal to ____________.
questions.question_html:
Let $f(x)=\int \frac{dx}{(3+4x^{2})\sqrt{4-3x^{2}}},|x|<\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ . If $f(0)=0$

and $f(1)=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}tan^{-1}(\frac{\alpha}{\beta})$ , $\alpha,\beta>0$ , then $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}$ is equal to ____________.
questions.explanation_html:
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\int \frac{dx}{(3+4x^{2})\sqrt{4-3x^{2}}} \\ \\ & x=\frac{1}{t} \\ \\ & =\int \frac{\frac{-1}{t^{2}}dt}{\frac{(3t^{2}+4)}{t^{2}}\frac{\sqrt{4t^{2}-3}}{t}} \\ \\ & =\int \frac{-dt \cdot t}{(3t^{2}+4)\sqrt{4t^{2}-3}}:\text{Put}4t^{2}-3=z^{2} \\ \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{zdz}{(3(\frac{z^{2}+3}{4})+4)z} \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{-dz}{3z^{2}+25}=-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dz}{z^{2}+(\frac{5}{\sqrt{3}})^{2}} \\ \\ & =-\frac{1}{3}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}tan^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{3}z}{5})+C \\ \\ & =-\frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\sqrt{4t^{2}-3})+C \\ \\ & f(x)=-\frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\sqrt{\frac{4-3x^{2}}{x^{2}}})+C \\ \\ & \because f(0)=0 \because c=\frac{\pi}{10\sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & f(1)=-\frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5})+\frac{\pi}{10\sqrt{3}} \\ \\ & f(1)=\frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}cot^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5})=\frac{1}{5\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}) \\ \\ & \alpha=5:\beta=\sqrt{3} \therefore \alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=28 \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: Let $I(x)=\int \sqrt{\frac{x+7}{x}}dx$ and $I(9)=12+7log_{e}7$ . If $I(1)=\alpha+7log_{e}(1+2\sqrt{2})$ , then $\alpha^{4}$ is equal to _________.
questions.question_html: Let $I(x)=\int \sqrt{\frac{x+7}{x}}dx$ and $I(9)=12+7log_{e}7$ . If $I(1)=\alpha+7log_{e}(1+2\sqrt{2})$ , then $\alpha^{4}$ is equal to _________.
questions.explanation_text: Given integral: $\int \sqrt{\frac{x+7}{x}}dx$ Let's make the substitution $x=t^{2}$ . Then, $dx=2tdt$ . Substituting these values, the integral becomes : $\int 2\sqrt{t^{2}+7}dt$ Now, let's evaluate this integral : $I(t)=2(\frac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^{2}+7}+\frac{7}{2}ln|t+\sqrt{t^{2}+7}|)+C$ Substituting back $t=\sqrt{x}$ , we have : $I(x)=2(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}\sqrt{x+7}+\frac{7}{2}ln|\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+7}|)+C$ Simplifying further : $I(x)=\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x+7}+7ln|\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+7}|+C$ We are given that $I(9)=12+7ln7$ . Let's substitute $x=9$ and solve for the constant $C$ : $12+7ln7=\sqrt{9}\sqrt{9+7}+7ln|\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{9+7}|+C$ $\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=3\sqrt{16}+7ln|\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{16}|+C$ $\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=3 \cdot 4+7ln(3+\sqrt{16})+C$ $\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=12+7ln(3+4)+C$ $\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=12+7ln7+C$ From this equation, we can see that $C=0$ . Now, we need to calculate $I(1)$ : $I(1)=\sqrt{1}\sqrt{1+7}+7ln|\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{1+7}|$ $\Rightarrow$ $I(1)=1\sqrt{8}+7ln(1+\sqrt{8})$ $\Rightarrow$ $I(1)=\sqrt{8}+7ln(1+2\sqrt{2})$ Therefore, $\alpha=\sqrt{8}$ . Finally, to find $\alpha^{4}$ : $\alpha^{4}=(\sqrt{8})^{4}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\alpha^{4}=8^{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $\alpha^{4}=64$ Hence, $\alpha^{4}$ is equal to 64.
questions.explanation_html:
Given integral: $\int \sqrt{\frac{x+7}{x}}dx$

Let's make the substitution $x=t^{2}$ . Then, $dx=2tdt$ .

Substituting these values, the integral becomes :

$\int 2\sqrt{t^{2}+7}dt$

Now, let's evaluate this integral :

$I(t)=2(\frac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^{2}+7}+\frac{7}{2}ln|t+\sqrt{t^{2}+7}|)+C$

Substituting back $t=\sqrt{x}$ , we have :

$I(x)=2(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}\sqrt{x+7}+\frac{7}{2}ln|\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+7}|)+C$

Simplifying further :

$I(x)=\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x+7}+7ln|\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{x+7}|+C$

We are given that $I(9)=12+7ln7$ .

Let's substitute $x=9$ and solve for the constant $C$ :

$12+7ln7=\sqrt{9}\sqrt{9+7}+7ln|\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{9+7}|+C$

$\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=3\sqrt{16}+7ln|\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{16}|+C$

$\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=3 \cdot 4+7ln(3+\sqrt{16})+C$

$\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=12+7ln(3+4)+C$

$\Rightarrow$ $12+7ln7=12+7ln7+C$

From this equation, we can see that $C=0$ .

Now, we need to calculate $I(1)$ :

$I(1)=\sqrt{1}\sqrt{1+7}+7ln|\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{1+7}|$

$\Rightarrow$ $I(1)=1\sqrt{8}+7ln(1+\sqrt{8})$

$\Rightarrow$ $I(1)=\sqrt{8}+7ln(1+2\sqrt{2})$

Therefore, $\alpha=\sqrt{8}$ .

Finally, to find $\alpha^{4}$ :

$\alpha^{4}=(\sqrt{8})^{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\alpha^{4}=8^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\alpha^{4}=64$

Hence, $\alpha^{4}$ is equal to 64.

questions.question_text: If $\int \frac{sinx}{sin^{3}x+cos^{3}x}dx=$ $\alpha log_{e}|1+tanx|+\beta log_{e}|1-tanx+tan^{2}x|+\gamma tan^{-1}(\frac{2tanx-1}{\sqrt{3}})+C$ , when C is constant of integration, then the value of $18(\alpha+\beta+\gamma^{2})$ is ______________.
questions.question_html:
If $\int \frac{sinx}{sin^{3}x+cos^{3}x}dx=$

$\alpha log_{e}|1+tanx|+\beta log_{e}|1-tanx+tan^{2}x|+\gamma tan^{-1}(\frac{2tanx-1}{\sqrt{3}})+C$ , when C is constant of integration, then the value of $18(\alpha+\beta+\gamma^{2})$ is ______________.
questions.explanation_text: $=\int \frac{\frac{sinx}{cos^{3}x}}{1+tan^{3}x}dx=\int \frac{tanx.sec^{2}x}{(tanx+1)(1+tan^{2}x-tanx)}dx$ Let $tanx=t \Rightarrow sec^{2}x.dx=dt$ $=\int \frac{t}{(t+1)(t^{2}-t+1)}dt$ $=\int (\frac{A}{t+1}+\frac{B(2t-1)}{t^{2}-t+1}+\frac{C}{t^{2}-t+1})dx$ $\Rightarrow A(t^{2}-t+1)+B(2t-1)(t^{2}-t+1)+C(t+1)=t$ $\Rightarrow t^{2}(A+2B)+t(-A+B+C)+A-B+C=1$ $\therefore$ $A+2B=0$ ..... (1) $-A+B+C=1$ ... (2) $A-B+C=0$ ... (3) $\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow A-B=-\frac{1}{2}$ ... (4) $A+2B=0$ $A-B=-\frac{1}{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $3B=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow B=\frac{1}{6}$ $A=-\frac{1}{3}$ $I=-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{1+t}+\frac{1}{6}\int \frac{2t-1}{t^{2}-t+1}dt+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{t^{2}-t+1}$ $=-\frac{1}{3}ln|(1+tanx)|+\frac{1}{6}ln|tan^{2}x-tanx+1|+\frac{1}{2}.\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{(tanx-\frac{1}{2})}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}})$ $=-\frac{1}{3}ln|(1+tanx)|+\frac{1}{6}ln|tan^{2}x-tanx+1|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{2tanx-1}{\sqrt{3}})+C$ $\alpha=-\frac{1}{3},\beta=\frac{1}{6},\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ $18(\alpha+\beta+\gamma^{2})=18(-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3})=3$
questions.explanation_html:
$=\int \frac{\frac{sinx}{cos^{3}x}}{1+tan^{3}x}dx=\int \frac{tanx.sec^{2}x}{(tanx+1)(1+tan^{2}x-tanx)}dx$

Let $tanx=t \Rightarrow sec^{2}x.dx=dt$

$=\int \frac{t}{(t+1)(t^{2}-t+1)}dt$

$=\int (\frac{A}{t+1}+\frac{B(2t-1)}{t^{2}-t+1}+\frac{C}{t^{2}-t+1})dx$

$\Rightarrow A(t^{2}-t+1)+B(2t-1)(t^{2}-t+1)+C(t+1)=t$

$\Rightarrow t^{2}(A+2B)+t(-A+B+C)+A-B+C=1$

$\therefore$ $A+2B=0$ ..... (1)

$-A+B+C=1$ ... (2)

$A-B+C=0$ ... (3)

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow A-B=-\frac{1}{2}$ ... (4)

$A+2B=0$

$A-B=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3B=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow B=\frac{1}{6}$

$A=-\frac{1}{3}$

$I=-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{1+t}+\frac{1}{6}\int \frac{2t-1}{t^{2}-t+1}dt+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{t^{2}-t+1}$

$=-\frac{1}{3}ln|(1+tanx)|+\frac{1}{6}ln|tan^{2}x-tanx+1|+\frac{1}{2}.\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{(tanx-\frac{1}{2})}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}})$

$=-\frac{1}{3}ln|(1+tanx)|+\frac{1}{6}ln|tan^{2}x-tanx+1|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{2tanx-1}{\sqrt{3}})+C$

$\alpha=-\frac{1}{3},\beta=\frac{1}{6},\gamma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$18(\alpha+\beta+\gamma^{2})=18(-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3})=3$

questions.question_html:
For real numbers $\alpha$ , $\beta$ , $\gamma$ and $\delta$ , if

questions.question_html: If $\int \frac{dx}{(x^{2}+x+1)^{2}}=atan^{-1}(\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}})+b(\frac{2x+1}{x^{2}+x+1})+C$ , x > 0 where C is the constant of integration, then the value of $9(\sqrt{3}a+b)$ is equal to _____________.
questions.explanation_text: $\int \frac{dx}{(x^{2}+x+1)^{2}}$ $=\int \frac{dx}{[(x+\frac{1}{2})^{2}+(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})^{2}]^{2}}$ Let $x+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}tan\theta$ $\Rightarrow dx=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}sec^{2}\theta d\theta$ $\therefore \int \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{\frac{9}{16}(tan^{2}\theta+1)^{2}}$ $=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\int \frac{sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{sec^{4}\theta}$ $=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\int cos^{2}\theta d\theta=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\int \frac{1+cos2\theta}{2}d\theta$ $=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}(\theta+\frac{sin2\theta}{2})+C$ = $\frac{4}{2\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}})+\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1+(\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}})^{2}}+C$ $=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{2x+1}{3})+\frac{1}{3}\frac{2x+1}{(x^{2}+x+1)}+C$ $\therefore a=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}},b=\frac{1}{3}$ Hence, $9(\sqrt{3}a+b)=9(\frac{4}{3}+\frac{1}{3})=15$
questions.explanation_html:
$\int \frac{dx}{(x^{2}+x+1)^{2}}$

$=\int \frac{dx}{[(x+\frac{1}{2})^{2}+(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})^{2}]^{2}}$

Let $x+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}tan\theta$

$\Rightarrow dx=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}sec^{2}\theta d\theta$

$\therefore \int \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{\frac{9}{16}(tan^{2}\theta+1)^{2}}$

$=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\int \frac{sec^{2}\theta d\theta}{sec^{4}\theta}$

$=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\int cos^{2}\theta d\theta=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\int \frac{1+cos2\theta}{2}d\theta$

$=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}(\theta+\frac{sin2\theta}{2})+C$

= $\frac{4}{2\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}})+\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1+(\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}})^{2}}+C$

$=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}}tan^{-1}(\frac{2x+1}{3})+\frac{1}{3}\frac{2x+1}{(x^{2}+x+1)}+C$

$\therefore a=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{3}},b=\frac{1}{3}$

Hence, $9(\sqrt{3}a+b)=9(\frac{4}{3}+\frac{1}{3})=15$

questions.question_html: $\int {\frac{(logx-1)}{1+(logx)^{2}}}^{2}dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation_text: $\int \frac{(logx-1)^{2}}{(1+(logx)^{2})^{2}}dx$ $=\int \frac{1+(logx)^{2}-2logx}{[1+(logx)^{2}]^{2}}$ $=\int [\frac{1}{(1+(logx)^{2})}-\frac{2logx}{(1+(logx)^{2})^{2}}]dx$ $=\int [\frac{e^{t}}{1+t^{2}}-\frac{2te^{t}}{(1+t^{2})^{2}}]dt$ put $logx=t \Rightarrow dx=e^{t}dt$ $=\int e^{t}[\frac{1}{1+t^{2}}-\frac{2t}{(1+t^{2})^{2}}]dt$ $[$ which is of the form $\int e^{x}(f(x)+f^{'}(x)dx)]$ $=\frac{e^{t}}{1+t^{2}}+c=\frac{x}{1+(logx)^{2}}+c$
questions.explanation_html:
$\int \frac{(logx-1)^{2}}{(1+(logx)^{2})^{2}}dx$

$=\int \frac{1+(logx)^{2}-2logx}{[1+(logx)^{2}]^{2}}$

$=\int [\frac{1}{(1+(logx)^{2})}-\frac{2logx}{(1+(logx)^{2})^{2}}]dx$

$=\int [\frac{e^{t}}{1+t^{2}}-\frac{2te^{t}}{(1+t^{2})^{2}}]dt$

put $logx=t \Rightarrow dx=e^{t}dt$

$=\int e^{t}[\frac{1}{1+t^{2}}-\frac{2t}{(1+t^{2})^{2}}]dt$

$[$ which is of the form

$\int e^{x}(f(x)+f^{'}(x)dx)]$

$=\frac{e^{t}}{1+t^{2}}+c=\frac{x}{1+(logx)^{2}}+c$
